narrative_arc: ordinary man argues with his girlfriend and a bully outside a wall -> she hands him a mysterious device -> he presses the button and undergoes an explosive muscle transformation -> full-body hero reveal as 'Omega' -> his girlfriend also reveals her own transformed super body and they celebrate together -> meanwhile the empowered bully turns violent, gloats, and breaks an ally out of police custody -> his power escalates to cosmic, planet-straddling scale (to be continued)

strengths: p3's single-panel stacked-silhouette growth timeline (5 staggered figures receding to a huge foreground flex) compresses a full transformation escalation into one bleed splash — a directly reusable 'ghost-trail' composite idea for CGI.

p1(cover B)/p20 panel1/p21 panels1&5 repeat a signature rear worm's-eye crossed-arm/glute shot four times across just 11 pages — proof this artist has a genuine go-to 'power entrance' staging worth stealing wholesale.
p4 stacks four back-to-back ECU money-shots (bicep, delt, forearm, glute) each with escalating SFX (ZRAAK->BULGE->SHKZROOM->THOOOOM) — a clean template for a rapid-fire growth-burst sequence.
p5, p10, and p41 all close their respective beats with a full-body 'reveal' splash at a low/worm's-eye angle — consistent payoff grammar the pipeline should copy for its own growth climaxes.
p41's literal planet-scale-comparison (figure straddling Earth) is the single boldest size-comparison device in the set — cheap to reproduce in CGI as a comped miniature-Earth prop.
weaknesses: p4's three tightest growth ECUs (panels 2-4) go completely faceless — the loudest SFX beats ('BULGE!!','SHKZROOM','THOOOOM') have zero face on screen, the same dead-face-during-peak-growth gap flagged elsewhere in the corpus.

p10's female transformation has no build-up shown in this delivery — it's a single 'BOOOM!' reveal with no escalation panels, the one-and-done pattern the rubric scores down (may be an artifact of the partial/non-contiguous sample rather than the full comic).
p2 leans on three flat-level, same-distance dialogue panels (1,3,5) before the trigger — the setup drags camera-wise even though the confrontation itself has stakes.
p20 panels 2-3 are plain flat-level talking-head reaction shots bracketing a much stronger foreshortened fist panel — a mid-page dip in dynamism.
Explicit sexual content on p11 (panels 3,6) leaves large parts of that page low-yield for the staging study beyond the two non-sexual flex panels.
